evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Apply, help define, and champion data warehouse governance: data quality, testing, documentation, coding best practices and peer reviews
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Strong rigour signals (governance, testing, documentation, peer reviews) coexist with at least two explicit velocity phrases ('We move fast', 'introduce step changes'), giving parity between the two, so mixed.
evidence.domain_risk: We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Payments/fintech company processing billions of transactions is a default-high-risk sector, and the role directly informs product performance metrics used across the business.
evidence.collaboration_width: product managers; product data scientists; data analysts and business teams
evidence.data_team_maturity: Take initiative to improve and optimise analytics engineering workflows and platforms
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A dedicated analytics engineering function with defined governance practices and multiple adjacent roles (product data scientists, data analysts) indicates a growing, mid-maturity data organisation.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design and implement high-performance, reusable, and scalable data models for our data warehouse using dbt and Snowflake
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Specific tools (dbt, Snowflake, Looker explores/views) and precise responsibilities give a technically grounded, hiring-manager-authored description.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: working closely with product managers and product data scientists to shape the product's evolution at Checkout
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Primary audience named in the role summary is product managers and product data scientists shaping product evolution, so product-oriented.
evidence.autonomy_level: You'll have end-to-end ownership of multiple data products from design to implementation to the operationalisation.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: End-to-end ownership and championing governance are strategic, but responsibilities also include executing scoped requests from data analysts/business teams, so mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tool usage or AI-data-infrastructure expectation is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Apply, help define, and champion data warehouse governance: data quality, testing, documentation, coding best practices and peer reviews
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data quality are framed as an owned, championed responsibility with explicit action verbs, not just listed tools.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Good attention to detail to highlight and address data quality issues
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data quality and governance are named responsibilities but sit alongside strong delivery/speed framing ('move fast', 'step changes'), so moderate rather than high.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: You'll have the opportunity to build new data products and introduce step changes in how we view analytics for these critical areas.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: JD emphasizes building new data products and introducing step changes rather than maintaining existing ones, so greenfield.
evidence.work_arrangement: Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.
evidence.loss_aversion: Apply, help define, and champion data warehouse governance: data quality, testing, documentation, coding best practices and peer reviews — governance framed as an owned responsibility but balanced against strong delivery-speed language elsewhere in the JD.
